## Nebraska 1099-C Cancellation of Debt [2026]: IRC 108, Form 982, and NE State Tax
Source: https://1099cdebt.com/states/nebraska.html

← 1099cdebt.com home

Nebraska 1099-C Cancellation of Debt [2026]: IRC 108, Form 982, and NE State Tax

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Nebraska residents.

What Is a 1099-C in Nebraska?

When a creditor cancels $600 or more of your debt, they are required by 26 U.S.C. 6050P to issue IRS Form 1099-C "Cancellation of Debt." Cancelled debt is generally treated as ordinary income under IRC 61(a)(11) - unless you qualify for an exclusion.

Nebraska follows federal guidance, but the state tax treatment depends on whether Nebraska's income tax code conforms to IRC 108.

Federal IRC 108 Exclusions (Apply in Nebraska)

ExclusionCode SectionNotes

Title 11 bankruptcyIRC 108(a)(1)(A)Debts discharged in Ch 7, 11, 13 are excluded. Use Form 982 box 1a.

Insolvency (outside BK)IRC 108(a)(1)(B)Excluded to extent liabilities exceed FMV of assets immediately before cancellation. Form 982 box 1b + worksheet.

Qualified farm indebtednessIRC 108(a)(1)(C)Narrow.

Qualified real property businessIRC 108(a)(1)(D)Narrow.

Qualified principal residenceIRC 108(a)(1)(E)Extended through 2025 by CAA; up to $750K principal mortgage forgiveness.

Student loan discharge (TPD / death / certain programs)IRC 108(f)ARPA extended through 2025 for most discharge contexts.

For most consumer credit card forgiveness / debt settlement outside bankruptcy, the insolvency exclusion is the workhorse. You calculate your total liabilities and total FMV of assets the day before cancellation and exclude up to the insolvency amount.

Nebraska State Income Tax Treatment of 1099-C Income

Nebraska posture: Conforms

What this means in practice:

If Nebraska conforms to IRC 108 (rolling or static), your bankruptcy or insolvency exclusion on the federal return flows through to your Nebraska return.

If Nebraska has no income tax, you owe no state tax on 1099-C income regardless of federal outcome.

If Nebraska is decoupled or static-conforming to an older IRC, you may need to add back or adjust on your Nebraska return. Nebraska DOR published guidance is the source of truth.

Form 982 Filing Guidance for Nebraska Taxpayers

Form 982 ("Reduction of Tax Attributes Due to Discharge of Indebtedness") is how you claim the exclusion on your federal return. Key boxes:

Box 1a - Discharge in a Title 11 case (bankruptcy). Always use this box if the debt was discharged in your Nebraska bankruptcy case.

Box 1b - Insolvency. Attach a worksheet showing total liabilities and total FMV of assets immediately before the cancellation.

Box 1e - Qualified principal residence indebtedness (QPRI).

Line 10a-10b - Reduction of basis in property (complex; often applies to QPRI).

For most Nebraska consumer-debt settlements, the 1b insolvency worksheet is the document that does the work. Preserve proof of liabilities and asset values as of the cancellation date.

1099-C Common Pitfalls in Nebraska

Received a 1099-C for old charged-off debt. Sometimes creditors issue 1099-Cs years after charge-off. The IRS "identifiable event" rules (Treas. Reg. 1.6050P-1) list eight triggering events. You may be able to contest the issuance if no true "discharge" occurred.

Zombie 1099-C. Debt buyer issues 1099-C then later tries to collect. IRS has informally indicated creditors cannot treat a debt as both cancelled (1099-C) and collectible, but courts are split.

Settled-debt 1099-C after Nebraska bankruptcy filed. If the debt was listed in your bankruptcy schedules, the Title 11 exclusion applies; creditor may still issue the 1099-C in error.

Spouse liability. Joint account 1099-C allocation can affect the insolvency worksheet; document separately-titled assets.

Nebraska Federal Bankruptcy Data

Nebraska filers frequently use bankruptcy specifically to avoid 1099-C tax exposure. Debts discharged in Title 11 are excluded from gross income under IRC 108(a)(1)(A) regardless of state conformity.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 75 consumer bankruptcy cases from Nebraska's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 757100.0%0.0%

Chapter 1318n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Nebraska Bankruptcy Beats Settlement for Tax Reasons

Example: Nebraska household with $43,020 in unsecured debt. Settlement at 50% = roughly $21,510 forgiven = potential ordinary income of the same amount. At 22% federal + Nebraska bracket, that is real money.

If the household is insolvent, the insolvency exclusion may cover most or all of it. But if the household has meaningful equity (home, retirement), insolvency exclusion may be limited - and the 1099-C tax exposure can exceed what bankruptcy legal fees would have cost.

The Title 11 exclusion is unconditional: any debt discharged in a Nebraska Chapter 7 or 13 case is excluded regardless of solvency.

Example: New Mexico household with $35,220 in unsecured debt. Settlement at 50% = roughly $17,610 forgiven = potential ordinary income of the same amount. At 22% federal + New Mexico bracket, that is real money.

If the household is insolvent, the insolvency exclusion may cover most or all of it. But if the household has meaningful equity (home, retirement), insolvency exclusion may be limited - and the 1099-C tax exposure can exceed what bankruptcy legal fees would have cost.

The Title 11 exclusion is unconditional: any debt discharged in a New Mexico Chapter 7 or 13 case is excluded regardless of solvency.

## New York 1099-C Cancellation of Debt [2026]: IRC 108, Form 982, and NY State Tax
Source: https://1099cdebt.com/states/new-york.html

← 1099cdebt.com home

New York 1099-C Cancellation of Debt [2026]: IRC 108, Form 982, and NY State Tax

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New York residents.

What Is a 1099-C in New York?

When a creditor cancels $600 or more of your debt, they are required by 26 U.S.C. 6050P to issue IRS Form 1099-C "Cancellation of Debt." Cancelled debt is generally treated as ordinary income under IRC 61(a)(11) - unless you qualify for an exclusion.

New York follows federal guidance, but the state tax treatment depends on whether New York's income tax code conforms to IRC 108.

Federal IRC 108 Exclusions (Apply in New York)

ExclusionCode SectionNotes

Title 11 bankruptcyIRC 108(a)(1)(A)Debts discharged in Ch 7, 11, 13 are excluded. Use Form 982 box 1a.

Insolvency (outside BK)IRC 108(a)(1)(B)Excluded to extent liabilities exceed FMV of assets immediately before cancellation. Form 982 box 1b + worksheet.

Qualified farm indebtednessIRC 108(a)(1)(C)Narrow.

Qualified real property businessIRC 108(a)(1)(D)Narrow.

Qualified principal residenceIRC 108(a)(1)(E)Extended through 2025 by CAA; up to $750K principal mortgage forgiveness.

Student loan discharge (TPD / death / certain programs)IRC 108(f)ARPA extended through 2025 for most discharge contexts.

For most consumer credit card forgiveness / debt settlement outside bankruptcy, the insolvency exclusion is the workhorse. You calculate your total liabilities and total FMV of assets the day before cancellation and exclude up to the insolvency amount.

New York State Income Tax Treatment of 1099-C Income

New York posture: Conforms

What this means in practice:

If New York conforms to IRC 108 (rolling or static), your bankruptcy or insolvency exclusion on the federal return flows through to your New York return.

If New York has no income tax, you owe no state tax on 1099-C income regardless of federal outcome.

If New York is decoupled or static-conforming to an older IRC, you may need to add back or adjust on your New York return. New York DOR published guidance is the source of truth.

Form 982 Filing Guidance for New York Taxpayers

Form 982 ("Reduction of Tax Attributes Due to Discharge of Indebtedness") is how you claim the exclusion on your federal return. Key boxes:

Box 1a - Discharge in a Title 11 case (bankruptcy). Always use this box if the debt was discharged in your New York bankruptcy case.

Box 1b - Insolvency. Attach a worksheet showing total liabilities and total FMV of assets immediately before the cancellation.

Box 1e - Qualified principal residence indebtedness (QPRI).

Line 10a-10b - Reduction of basis in property (complex; often applies to QPRI).

For most New York consumer-debt settlements, the 1b insolvency worksheet is the document that does the work. Preserve proof of liabilities and asset values as of the cancellation date.

1099-C Common Pitfalls in New York

Received a 1099-C for old charged-off debt. Sometimes creditors issue 1099-Cs years after charge-off. The IRS "identifiable event" rules (Treas. Reg. 1.6050P-1) list eight triggering events. You may be able to contest the issuance if no true "discharge" occurred.

Zombie 1099-C. Debt buyer issues 1099-C then later tries to collect. IRS has informally indicated creditors cannot treat a debt as both cancelled (1099-C) and collectible, but courts are split.

Settled-debt 1099-C after New York bankruptcy filed. If the debt was listed in your bankruptcy schedules, the Title 11 exclusion applies; creditor may still issue the 1099-C in error.

Spouse liability. Joint account 1099-C allocation can affect the insolvency worksheet; document separately-titled assets.

New York Federal Bankruptcy Data

New York filers frequently use bankruptcy specifically to avoid 1099-C tax exposure. Debts discharged in Title 11 are excluded from gross income under IRC 108(a)(1)(A) regardless of state conformity.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,231 consumer bankruptcy cases from New York's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 71,14598.7%1.2%

Chapter 138628.2%71.8%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When New York Bankruptcy Beats Settlement for Tax Reasons

Example: New York household with $48,840 in unsecured debt. Settlement at 50% = roughly $24,420 forgiven = potential ordinary income of the same amount. At 22% federal + New York bracket, that is real money.

If the household is insolvent, the insolvency exclusion may cover most or all of it. But if the household has meaningful equity (home, retirement), insolvency exclusion may be limited - and the 1099-C tax exposure can exceed what bankruptcy legal fees would have cost.

The Title 11 exclusion is unconditional: any debt discharged in a New York Chapter 7 or 13 case is excluded regardless of solvency.

Federal IRC 108 Exclusions (Apply in Oregon)

ExclusionCode SectionNotes

Title 11 bankruptcyIRC 108(a)(1)(A)Debts discharged in Ch 7, 11, 13 are excluded. Use Form 982 box 1a.

Insolvency (outside BK)IRC 108(a)(1)(B)Excluded to extent liabilities exceed FMV of assets immediately before cancellation. Form 982 box 1b + worksheet.

Qualified farm indebtednessIRC 108(a)(1)(C)Narrow.

Qualified real property businessIRC 108(a)(1)(D)Narrow.

Qualified principal residenceIRC 108(a)(1)(E)Extended through 2025 by CAA; up to $750K principal mortgage forgiveness.

Student loan discharge (TPD / death / certain programs)IRC 108(f)ARPA extended through 2025 for most discharge contexts.

For most consumer credit card forgiveness / debt settlement outside bankruptcy, the insolvency exclusion is the workhorse. You calculate your total liabilities and total FMV of assets the day before cancellation and exclude up to the insolvency amount.

Oregon State Income Tax Treatment of 1099-C Income

Oregon posture: Conforms

What this means in practice:

If Oregon conforms to IRC 108 (rolling or static), your bankruptcy or insolvency exclusion on the federal return flows through to your Oregon return.

If Oregon has no income tax, you owe no state tax on 1099-C income regardless of federal outcome.

If Oregon is decoupled or static-conforming to an older IRC, you may need to add back or adjust on your Oregon return. Oregon DOR published guidance is the source of truth.

Form 982 Filing Guidance for Oregon Taxpayers

Form 982 ("Reduction of Tax Attributes Due to Discharge of Indebtedness") is how you claim the exclusion on your federal return. Key boxes:

Box 1a - Discharge in a Title 11 case (bankruptcy). Always use this box if the debt was discharged in your Oregon bankruptcy case.

Box 1b - Insolvency. Attach a worksheet showing total liabilities and total FMV of assets immediately before the cancellation.

Box 1e - Qualified principal residence indebtedness (QPRI).

Line 10a-10b - Reduction of basis in property (complex; often applies to QPRI).

For most Oregon consumer-debt settlements, the 1b insolvency worksheet is the document that does the work. Preserve proof of liabilities and asset values as of the cancellation date.

1099-C Common Pitfalls in Oregon

Received a 1099-C for old charged-off debt. Sometimes creditors issue 1099-Cs years after charge-off. The IRS "identifiable event" rules (Treas. Reg. 1.6050P-1) list eight triggering events. You may be able to contest the issuance if no true "discharge" occurred.

Zombie 1099-C. Debt buyer issues 1099-C then later tries to collect. IRS has informally indicated creditors cannot treat a debt as both cancelled (1099-C) and collectible, but courts are split.

Settled-debt 1099-C after Oregon bankruptcy filed. If the debt was listed in your bankruptcy schedules, the Title 11 exclusion applies; creditor may still issue the 1099-C in error.

Spouse liability. Joint account 1099-C allocation can affect the insolvency worksheet; document separately-titled assets.

When Oregon Bankruptcy Beats Settlement for Tax Reasons

Example: Oregon household with $45,840 in unsecured debt. Settlement at 50% = roughly $22,920 forgiven = potential ordinary income of the same amount. At 22% federal + Oregon bracket, that is real money.

If the household is insolvent, the insolvency exclusion may cover most or all of it. But if the household has meaningful equity (home, retirement), insolvency exclusion may be limited - and the 1099-C tax exposure can exceed what bankruptcy legal fees would have cost.

The Title 11 exclusion is unconditional: any debt discharged in a Oregon Chapter 7 or 13 case is excluded regardless of solvency.

Related Oregon Resources

## Pennsylvania 1099-C Cancellation of Debt [2026]: IRC 108, Form 982, and PA State Tax
Source: https://1099cdebt.com/states/pennsylvania.html

← 1099cdebt.com home

Pennsylvania 1099-C Cancellation of Debt [2026]: IRC 108, Form 982, and PA State Tax

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Pennsylvania residents.

What Is a 1099-C in Pennsylvania?

When a creditor cancels $600 or more of your debt, they are required by 26 U.S.C. 6050P to issue IRS Form 1099-C "Cancellation of Debt." Cancelled debt is generally treated as ordinary income under IRC 61(a)(11) - unless you qualify for an exclusion.

Pennsylvania follows federal guidance, but the state tax treatment depends on whether Pennsylvania's income tax code conforms to IRC 108.

Federal IRC 108 Exclusions (Apply in Pennsylvania)

ExclusionCode SectionNotes

Title 11 bankruptcyIRC 108(a)(1)(A)Debts discharged in Ch 7, 11, 13 are excluded. Use Form 982 box 1a.

Insolvency (outside BK)IRC 108(a)(1)(B)Excluded to extent liabilities exceed FMV of assets immediately before cancellation. Form 982 box 1b + worksheet.

Qualified farm indebtednessIRC 108(a)(1)(C)Narrow.

Qualified real property businessIRC 108(a)(1)(D)Narrow.

Qualified principal residenceIRC 108(a)(1)(E)Extended through 2025 by CAA; up to $750K principal mortgage forgiveness.

Student loan discharge (TPD / death / certain programs)IRC 108(f)ARPA extended through 2025 for most discharge contexts.

For most consumer credit card forgiveness / debt settlement outside bankruptcy, the insolvency exclusion is the workhorse. You calculate your total liabilities and total FMV of assets the day before cancellation and exclude up to the insolvency amount.

Pennsylvania State Income Tax Treatment of 1099-C Income

Pennsylvania posture: Decoupled (PIT does not tax COD in most consumer contexts)

What this means in practice:

If Pennsylvania conforms to IRC 108 (rolling or static), your bankruptcy or insolvency exclusion on the federal return flows through to your Pennsylvania return.

If Pennsylvania has no income tax, you owe no state tax on 1099-C income regardless of federal outcome.

If Pennsylvania is decoupled or static-conforming to an older IRC, you may need to add back or adjust on your Pennsylvania return. Pennsylvania DOR published guidance is the source of truth.

Form 982 Filing Guidance for Pennsylvania Taxpayers

Form 982 ("Reduction of Tax Attributes Due to Discharge of Indebtedness") is how you claim the exclusion on your federal return. Key boxes:

Box 1a - Discharge in a Title 11 case (bankruptcy). Always use this box if the debt was discharged in your Pennsylvania bankruptcy case.

Box 1b - Insolvency. Attach a worksheet showing total liabilities and total FMV of assets immediately before the cancellation.

Box 1e - Qualified principal residence indebtedness (QPRI).

Line 10a-10b - Reduction of basis in property (complex; often applies to QPRI).

For most Pennsylvania consumer-debt settlements, the 1b insolvency worksheet is the document that does the work. Preserve proof of liabilities and asset values as of the cancellation date.

1099-C Common Pitfalls in Pennsylvania

Received a 1099-C for old charged-off debt. Sometimes creditors issue 1099-Cs years after charge-off. The IRS "identifiable event" rules (Treas. Reg. 1.6050P-1) list eight triggering events. You may be able to contest the issuance if no true "discharge" occurred.

Zombie 1099-C. Debt buyer issues 1099-C then later tries to collect. IRS has informally indicated creditors cannot treat a debt as both cancelled (1099-C) and collectible, but courts are split.

Settled-debt 1099-C after Pennsylvania bankruptcy filed. If the debt was listed in your bankruptcy schedules, the Title 11 exclusion applies; creditor may still issue the 1099-C in error.

Spouse liability. Joint account 1099-C allocation can affect the insolvency worksheet; document separately-titled assets.

Pennsylvania Federal Bankruptcy Data

Pennsylvania filers frequently use bankruptcy specifically to avoid 1099-C tax exposure. Debts discharged in Title 11 are excluded from gross income under IRC 108(a)(1)(A) regardless of state conformity.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 1,513 consumer bankruptcy cases from Pennsylvania's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7415n/an/a

Chapter 131,098n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Pennsylvania Bankruptcy Beats Settlement for Tax Reasons

Example: Pennsylvania household with $43,920 in unsecured debt. Settlement at 50% = roughly $21,960 forgiven = potential ordinary income of the same amount. At 22% federal + Pennsylvania bracket, that is real money.

If the household is insolvent, the insolvency exclusion may cover most or all of it. But if the household has meaningful equity (home, retirement), insolvency exclusion may be limited - and the 1099-C tax exposure can exceed what bankruptcy legal fees would have cost.

The Title 11 exclusion is unconditional: any debt discharged in a Pennsylvania Chapter 7 or 13 case is excluded regardless of solvency.

Example: Tennessee household with $38,400 in unsecured debt. Settlement at 50% = roughly $19,200 forgiven = potential ordinary income of the same amount. At 22% federal + Tennessee bracket, that is real money.

If the household is insolvent, the insolvency exclusion may cover most or all of it. But if the household has meaningful equity (home, retirement), insolvency exclusion may be limited - and the 1099-C tax exposure can exceed what bankruptcy legal fees would have cost.

The Title 11 exclusion is unconditional: any debt discharged in a Tennessee Chapter 7 or 13 case is excluded regardless of solvency.

## Texas 1099-C Cancellation of Debt [2026]: IRC 108, Form 982, and TX State Tax
Source: https://1099cdebt.com/states/texas.html

← 1099cdebt.com home

Texas 1099-C Cancellation of Debt [2026]: IRC 108, Form 982, and TX State Tax

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Texas residents.

What Is a 1099-C in Texas?

When a creditor cancels $600 or more of your debt, they are required by 26 U.S.C. 6050P to issue IRS Form 1099-C "Cancellation of Debt." Cancelled debt is generally treated as ordinary income under IRC 61(a)(11) - unless you qualify for an exclusion.

Texas follows federal guidance, but the state tax treatment depends on whether Texas's income tax code conforms to IRC 108.

Federal IRC 108 Exclusions (Apply in Texas)

ExclusionCode SectionNotes

Title 11 bankruptcyIRC 108(a)(1)(A)Debts discharged in Ch 7, 11, 13 are excluded. Use Form 982 box 1a.

Insolvency (outside BK)IRC 108(a)(1)(B)Excluded to extent liabilities exceed FMV of assets immediately before cancellation. Form 982 box 1b + worksheet.

Qualified farm indebtednessIRC 108(a)(1)(C)Narrow.

Qualified real property businessIRC 108(a)(1)(D)Narrow.

Qualified principal residenceIRC 108(a)(1)(E)Extended through 2025 by CAA; up to $750K principal mortgage forgiveness.

Student loan discharge (TPD / death / certain programs)IRC 108(f)ARPA extended through 2025 for most discharge contexts.

For most consumer credit card forgiveness / debt settlement outside bankruptcy, the insolvency exclusion is the workhorse. You calculate your total liabilities and total FMV of assets the day before cancellation and exclude up to the insolvency amount.

Texas State Income Tax Treatment of 1099-C Income

Texas posture: No income tax

What this means in practice:

If Texas conforms to IRC 108 (rolling or static), your bankruptcy or insolvency exclusion on the federal return flows through to your Texas return.

If Texas has no income tax, you owe no state tax on 1099-C income regardless of federal outcome.

If Texas is decoupled or static-conforming to an older IRC, you may need to add back or adjust on your Texas return. Texas DOR published guidance is the source of truth.

Form 982 Filing Guidance for Texas Taxpayers

Form 982 ("Reduction of Tax Attributes Due to Discharge of Indebtedness") is how you claim the exclusion on your federal return. Key boxes:

Box 1a - Discharge in a Title 11 case (bankruptcy). Always use this box if the debt was discharged in your Texas bankruptcy case.

Box 1b - Insolvency. Attach a worksheet showing total liabilities and total FMV of assets immediately before the cancellation.

Box 1e - Qualified principal residence indebtedness (QPRI).

Line 10a-10b - Reduction of basis in property (complex; often applies to QPRI).

For most Texas consumer-debt settlements, the 1b insolvency worksheet is the document that does the work. Preserve proof of liabilities and asset values as of the cancellation date.

1099-C Common Pitfalls in Texas

Received a 1099-C for old charged-off debt. Sometimes creditors issue 1099-Cs years after charge-off. The IRS "identifiable event" rules (Treas. Reg. 1.6050P-1) list eight triggering events. You may be able to contest the issuance if no true "discharge" occurred.

Zombie 1099-C. Debt buyer issues 1099-C then later tries to collect. IRS has informally indicated creditors cannot treat a debt as both cancelled (1099-C) and collectible, but courts are split.

Settled-debt 1099-C after Texas bankruptcy filed. If the debt was listed in your bankruptcy schedules, the Title 11 exclusion applies; creditor may still issue the 1099-C in error.

Spouse liability. Joint account 1099-C allocation can affect the insolvency worksheet; document separately-titled assets.

Texas Federal Bankruptcy Data

Texas filers frequently use bankruptcy specifically to avoid 1099-C tax exposure. Debts discharged in Title 11 are excluded from gross income under IRC 108(a)(1)(A) regardless of state conformity.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 30,781 consumer bankruptcy cases from Texas's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 711,84497.8%2.0%

Chapter 1318,93736.8%63.2%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When Texas Bankruptcy Beats Settlement for Tax Reasons

Example: Texas household with $43,800 in unsecured debt. Settlement at 50% = roughly $21,900 forgiven = potential ordinary income of the same amount. At 22% federal + Texas bracket, that is real money.

If the household is insolvent, the insolvency exclusion may cover most or all of it. But if the household has meaningful equity (home, retirement), insolvency exclusion may be limited - and the 1099-C tax exposure can exceed what bankruptcy legal fees would have cost.

The Title 11 exclusion is unconditional: any debt discharged in a Texas Chapter 7 or 13 case is excluded regardless of solvency.

If West Virginia is decoupled or static-conforming to an older IRC, you may need to add back or adjust on your West Virginia return. West Virginia DOR published guidance is the source of truth.

Form 982 Filing Guidance for West Virginia Taxpayers

Form 982 ("Reduction of Tax Attributes Due to Discharge of Indebtedness") is how you claim the exclusion on your federal return. Key boxes:

Box 1a - Discharge in a Title 11 case (bankruptcy). Always use this box if the debt was discharged in your West Virginia bankruptcy case.

Box 1b - Insolvency. Attach a worksheet showing total liabilities and total FMV of assets immediately before the cancellation.

Box 1e - Qualified principal residence indebtedness (QPRI).

Line 10a-10b - Reduction of basis in property (complex; often applies to QPRI).

For most West Virginia consumer-debt settlements, the 1b insolvency worksheet is the document that does the work. Preserve proof of liabilities and asset values as of the cancellation date.

1099-C Common Pitfalls in West Virginia

Received a 1099-C for old charged-off debt. Sometimes creditors issue 1099-Cs years after charge-off. The IRS "identifiable event" rules (Treas. Reg. 1.6050P-1) list eight triggering events. You may be able to contest the issuance if no true "discharge" occurred.

Zombie 1099-C. Debt buyer issues 1099-C then later tries to collect. IRS has informally indicated creditors cannot treat a debt as both cancelled (1099-C) and collectible, but courts are split.

Settled-debt 1099-C after West Virginia bankruptcy filed. If the debt was listed in your bankruptcy schedules, the Title 11 exclusion applies; creditor may still issue the 1099-C in error.

Spouse liability. Joint account 1099-C allocation can affect the insolvency worksheet; document separately-titled assets.

West Virginia Federal Bankruptcy Data

West Virginia filers frequently use bankruptcy specifically to avoid 1099-C tax exposure. Debts discharged in Title 11 are excluded from gross income under IRC 108(a)(1)(A) regardless of state conformity.

Numbers below come from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 60 consumer bankruptcy cases from West Virginia's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCases FiledDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 75498.1%1.9%

Chapter 136n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

When West Virginia Bankruptcy Beats Settlement for Tax Reasons

Example: West Virginia household with $33,120 in unsecured debt. Settlement at 50% = roughly $16,560 forgiven = potential ordinary income of the same amount. At 22% federal + West Virginia bracket, that is real money.

If the household is insolvent, the insolvency exclusion may cover most or all of it. But if the household has meaningful equity (home, retirement), insolvency exclusion may be limited - and the 1099-C tax exposure can exceed what bankruptcy legal fees would have cost.

The Title 11 exclusion is unconditional: any debt discharged in a West Virginia Chapter 7 or 13 case is excluded regardless of solvency.

## Wisconsin 1099-C Cancellation of Debt [2026]: IRC 108, Form 982, and WI State Tax
Source: https://1099cdebt.com/states/wisconsin.html

← 1099cdebt.com home

Wisconsin 1099-C Cancellation of Debt [2026]: IRC 108, Form 982, and WI State Tax

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Wisconsin residents.

What Is a 1099-C in Wisconsin?

When a creditor cancels $600 or more of your debt, they are required by 26 U.S.C. 6050P to issue IRS Form 1099-C "Cancellation of Debt." Cancelled debt is generally treated as ordinary income under IRC 61(a)(11) - unless you qualify for an exclusion.

Wisconsin follows federal guidance, but the state tax treatment depends on whether Wisconsin's income tax code conforms to IRC 108.

Federal IRC 108 Exclusions (Apply in Wisconsin)

ExclusionCode SectionNotes

Title 11 bankruptcyIRC 108(a)(1)(A)Debts discharged in Ch 7, 11, 13 are excluded. Use Form 982 box 1a.

Insolvency (outside BK)IRC 108(a)(1)(B)Excluded to extent liabilities exceed FMV of assets immediately before cancellation. Form 982 box 1b + worksheet.

Qualified farm indebtednessIRC 108(a)(1)(C)Narrow.

Qualified real property businessIRC 108(a)(1)(D)Narrow.

Qualified principal residenceIRC 108(a)(1)(E)Extended through 2025 by CAA; up to $750K principal mortgage forgiveness.

Student loan discharge (TPD / death / certain programs)IRC 108(f)ARPA extended through 2025 for most discharge contexts.

For most consumer credit card forgiveness / debt settlement outside bankruptcy, the insolvency exclusion is the workhorse. You calculate your total liabilities and total FMV of assets the day before cancellation and exclude up to the insolvency amount.

Wisconsin State Income Tax Treatment of 1099-C Income

Wisconsin posture: Static conform

What this means in practice:

If Wisconsin conforms to IRC 108 (rolling or static), your bankruptcy or insolvency exclusion on the federal return flows through to your Wisconsin return.

If Wisconsin has no income tax, you owe no state tax on 1099-C income regardless of federal outcome.

If Wisconsin is decoupled or static-conforming to an older IRC, you may need to add back or adjust on your Wisconsin return. Wisconsin DOR published guidance is the source of truth.

Form 982 Filing Guidance for Wisconsin Taxpayers

Form 982 ("Reduction of Tax Attributes Due to Discharge of Indebtedness") is how you claim the exclusion on your federal return. Key boxes:

Box 1a - Discharge in a Title 11 case (bankruptcy). Always use this box if the debt was discharged in your Wisconsin bankruptcy case.

Box 1b - Insolvency. Attach a worksheet showing total liabilities and total FMV of assets immediately before the cancellation.

Box 1e - Qualified principal residence indebtedness (QPRI).

Line 10a-10b - Reduction of basis in property (complex; often applies to QPRI).

For most Wisconsin consumer-debt settlements, the 1b insolvency worksheet is the document that does the work. Preserve proof of liabilities and asset values as of the cancellation date.

Received a 1099-C for old charged-off debt. Sometimes creditors issue 1099-Cs years after charge-off. The IRS "identifiable event" rules (Treas. Reg. 1.6050P-1) list eight triggering events. You may be able to contest the issuance if no true "discharge" occurred.

Zombie 1099-C. Debt buyer issues 1099-C then later tries to collect. IRS has informally indicated creditors cannot treat a debt as both cancelled (1099-C) and collectible, but courts are split.

Spouse liability. Joint account 1099-C allocation can affect the insolvency worksheet; document separately-titled assets.

## Additional FAQ Pages


### Do I have to pay taxes on a 1099-C? - 1099-C Cancelled Debt Tax Guide
Source: https://1099cdebt.com/paa/do-i-have-to-pay-taxes-on-a-1099-c.html

Skip to content

1099cdebt.com

Home
Questions

Home › Common Questions › Do I have to pay taxes on a 1099-C?

People Also Ask

Do I have to pay taxes on a 1099-C?

Generally yes - cancelled debt is taxable income. However, major exclusions exist: you owe no taxes if you were insolvent (debts exceeded assets) at the time of cancellation, if the debt was discharged in bankruptcy, or if it was qualified principal residence debt. File IRS Form 982 to claim any exclusion.

Receiving a 1099-C does not automatically mean you owe taxes. Several exclusions can eliminate the tax liability entirely.

When Cancelled Debt IS Taxable

Under IRC Section 61(a)(11), cancelled debt is included in gross income. If a creditor cancels $10,000 of your debt and you do not qualify for any exclusion, the IRS treats that $10,000 as income, and you owe taxes on it at your marginal rate.

Exclusions Under IRC Section 108

Insolvency exclusion: If your total liabilities exceeded your total assets at the time the debt was cancelled, you were insolvent. You can exclude cancelled debt up to the amount of your insolvency. This is the most commonly used exclusion.

Bankruptcy exclusion: Debt discharged in a Title 11 bankruptcy case is fully excluded. No dollar limit.

Qualified principal residence debt: Up to $750,000 of forgiven mortgage debt on your primary home may be excluded (extended through 2025 by the Mortgage Forgiveness Debt Relief Act).

Qualified farm debt

Qualified real property business debt

How to Claim the Exclusion

File IRS Form 982 (Reduction of Tax Attributes Due to Discharge of Indebtedness) with your tax return. Check the appropriate box for your exclusion, enter the excluded amount, and attach it to your Form 1040. Even if the exclusion covers the entire amount, you must still file Form 982 to avoid IRS notices.

If you are unsure whether you qualify for an exclusion, calculate your assets and liabilities as of the cancellation date. If liabilities exceeded assets by any amount, you have at least a partial insolvency exclusion available.

### Common Questions - 1099-C Cancelled Debt Tax Guide
Source: https://1099cdebt.com/paa/index.html

1099cdebt.com

Home
Questions

Common Questions

Clear, data-backed answers to the most frequently asked questions

Do I have to pay taxes on a 1099-C?

What is the insolvency exclusion for cancelled debt?

Tax Implications of Bankruptcy and Debt Cancellation

The intersection of bankruptcy and tax law creates important planning opportunities. Debt discharged in bankruptcy is excluded from taxable income under IRC Section 108(a)(1)(A), but you must properly report the exclusion using IRS Form 982. Outside of bankruptcy, cancelled debt is generally taxable income, though the insolvency exclusion under IRC Section 108(a)(1)(B) can eliminate or reduce the tax liability if your debts exceeded your assets at the time of cancellation.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does bankruptcy clear tax debt?

Some tax debts can be discharged in bankruptcy if they meet specific criteria: the tax return was due more than 3 years ago, was filed more than 2 years ago, and was assessed more than 240 days ago. Fraud penalties and trust fund taxes (withheld payroll taxes) generally cannot be discharged.

Will I get a 1099-C after bankruptcy?

Creditors may still issue a 1099-C for cancelled debt even after a bankruptcy discharge. However, debt discharged in bankruptcy is excluded from taxable income under IRC Section 108. File IRS Form 982 with your tax return to claim the exclusion. Keep your discharge order as documentation.

Do I need to file tax returns before filing bankruptcy?

Yes. You must be current on tax filings for at least the past 4 years before filing bankruptcy. The bankruptcy trustee will request copies of recent returns, and failure to provide them can result in dismissal of your case. Filing returns is also a prerequisite for discharging older tax debts.

### What is the insolvency exclusion for cancelled debt? - 1099-C Cancelled Debt Tax Guide
Source: https://1099cdebt.com/paa/what-is-the-insolvency-exclusion-for-cancelled-debt.html

Skip to content

1099cdebt.com

Home
Questions

Home › Common Questions › What is the insolvency exclusion for cancelled debt?

People Also Ask

What is the insolvency exclusion for cancelled debt?

The insolvency exclusion lets you exclude cancelled debt from income if your total debts exceeded your total assets at the time of cancellation. You can exclude cancelled debt up to the amount you were insolvent. For example, if your debts exceeded assets by $20,000 and $15,000 was cancelled, the entire $15,000 is excluded.

The insolvency exclusion under IRC Section 108(a)(1)(B) is the most commonly used exclusion for 1099-C income and is available to anyone regardless of whether they filed bankruptcy.

How to Calculate Insolvency

Insolvency is calculated immediately before the debt cancellation:

List all assets: Bank accounts, investments, real estate (fair market value), vehicles, personal property, retirement accounts (in some cases)

List all liabilities: All debts including mortgages, car loans, credit cards, student loans, medical debt, tax debt

Calculate: Total Liabilities minus Total Assets = Insolvency Amount

Example

Total assets: $50,000. Total liabilities: $80,000. Insolvency amount: $30,000. If a creditor cancels $25,000 of debt, the entire $25,000 is excluded because it is less than the $30,000 insolvency amount. If $35,000 was cancelled, only $30,000 would be excluded, and $5,000 would be taxable.

What Counts as an Asset?

The IRS includes virtually everything you own: cash, bank balances, real estate equity, vehicle value, investment accounts, business interests, and personal property. Whether retirement accounts count is debated - some tax professionals exclude ERISA-protected retirement accounts from the calculation, which can increase your insolvency amount.

Filing the Exclusion

Report the exclusion on IRS Form 982, checking box 1b (insolvency). Enter the excluded amount on line 2. Note that the exclusion may require reducing certain "tax attributes" (NOLs, credits, basis) as specified in Section 108(b), but for most individuals this has no practical impact.
